symptom: PC0 (VLAN 10) can ping its own gateway but cannot reach PC5 (VLAN 20) even though both VLANs exist on the switch.
topology: PC0(VLAN10) -- SW1 -- Router0(sub-int Gi0/0.10, Gi0/0.20) -- SW1 -- PC5(VLAN20)
show_ip_interface_brief:
Interface IP-Address OK? Method Status Protocol
GigabitEthernet0/0.10 192.168.10.1 YES manual up up
GigabitEthernet0/0.20 192.168.20.1 YES manual up up
show_ip_route:
C 192.168.10.0/24 is directly connected, GigabitEthernet0/0.10
C 192.168.20.0/24 is directly connected, GigabitEthernet0/0.20
show_vlan_brief:
VLAN Name Status Ports
10 STUDENTS active Fa0/1, Fa0/2
20 STAFF active Fa0/3
extra_evidence: show interfaces trunk shows Fa0/1-3 access mode, no trunk configured between SW1 and Router0.
expected_fault: Router-on-a-stick trunk missing: the switch port toward Router0 is in access mode, so 802.1Q tagged inter-VLAN traffic is dropped.

symptom: New PC plugged into Fa0/5 gets no VLAN connectivity; interface shows up/up but device can't reach anything on VLAN 30.

show_vlan_brief:
VLAN Name Status Ports
1 default active Fa0/5
30 SALES active Fa0/6
extra_evidence: Fa0/5 is still assigned to VLAN 1 (default) instead of VLAN 30.
expected_fault: Access port Fa0/5 was never moved into VLAN 30, so the PC lands on the default VLAN.

symptom: All VLAN 40 (guest) devices on SW3 can talk to each other but nothing on the rest of the network — including the gateway.

expected_fault: VLAN 40 is pruned from the trunk between SW3 and SW1, so guest traffic never reaches the router.

symptom: PC on VLAN 10 intermittently loses connectivity to the gateway; SW1 console is showing repeated topology change notifications.
topology: PC1 -- SW1 -- SW4 (redundant link, no STP tuning) -- Router0
show_ip_interface_brief:
Interface IP-Address OK? Method Status Protocol
GigabitEthernet0/0.10 192.168.10.1 YES manual up up

extra_evidence: show spanning-tree vlan 10 shows frequent root port changes between SW1 and SW4 (redundant link, PortFast misconfigured on a trunk port).
expected_fault: Spanning-tree instability on VLAN 10 caused by a misconfigured PortFast trunk port creating an intermittent loop/re-convergence.

symptom: After adding a new 'permit' line to an ACL, guest VLAN traffic to the internet stopped completely.

expected_fault: The new permit rule was added after an existing 'deny ip any any', so it never takes effect and all guest traffic is denied.

symptom: Server0 cannot send DNS responses back to clients even though the DNS service is confirmed running and reachable inbound.

symptom: Only one internal PC at a time can reach the internet; a second PC's traffic silently fails while the first is active.

expected_fault: NAT pool is configured without 'overload' (PAT), so only one internal host can be translated to the single public address at a time.

symptom: External users cannot reach the internally-hosted web server via the public IP, even though NAT overload for outbound traffic works fine.

expected_fault: Outbound PAT/overload is configured, but there is no static NAT/port-forward rule exposing Server0's port 80 to the public interface.

symptom: Wireless clients near the far end of the building repeatedly disconnect and reconnect, wired clients are unaffected.
extra_evidence: AP2 and AP3 (in the adjacent room) are both configured on channel 6 with high power, causing co-channel interference at the overlap zone.

symptom: A specific laptop cannot associate with the AP at all, error says 'network security key mismatch', while all other devices connect fine.
extra_evidence: AP0 is configured for WPA2-PSK, but the specific laptop's wireless adapter is manually set to WEP (leftover config from a different network).
expected_fault: The laptop's wireless adapter is configured for WEP security while the AP uses WPA2-PSK — a security-mode mismatch.
